company: Elevate Campuses Limited (formerly Good Host Spaces Limited)
about: Elevate Campuses owns, operates and manages on-campus student accommodation at higher education institutions in India and owns K-12 school assets in India and Dubai. As of Mar-2026 it has 20,368 owned beds and 55,487 managed beds across 14 student accommodation campuses, under the Good Host Spaces and ScholarZ brands. It is backed by Hillhouse-linked promoter entities and plans to buy 14 K-12 school entities from fellow promoter subsidiaries with IPO money.
sector: Education infrastructure / Student accommodation and K-12 real estate

objects.purpose: Purchase consideration for acquiring 14 K-12 school entities and campuses from fellow subsidiaries of the Promoters
Repayment/prepayment of borrowings of the Company and subsidiaries (GHS Shoolini, GHS Sonipat, Data Ram Sons, Souk HIS UAE, Souk NLCS UAE)
Unidentified acquisitions, strategic initiatives and general corporate purposes (capped at 35% of gross proceeds)

names: Genius Rajkot Investment Holdings Pte. Ltd.
promoters.background: Promoters are ultimately owned and controlled by funds of Hillhouse Investment, a large global alternative asset manager.

concentration.note: Three largest HEIs gave 61.46% of FY26 revenue (89.00% in FY25, 88.60% in FY24); 70.13% of FY26 revenue came from northern and southern India.

litigation_note: Contingent liabilities of Rs 37.34 crore (GST Rs 37.22 crore, income tax Rs 0.12 crore) at Mar-26. GST show-cause notices of Rs 49.61 crore (holding company, demand order Rs 9.68 crore issued) and Rs 31.46 crore (GHS Shoolini) are not provided for; management believes it has a strong case.
strengths: Largest independent on-campus student housing platform in India: 78,542 beds as of June 2026, about 2.1 times the next largest player per CBRE.
Owned-bed occupancy of 89.37% in AY2025-26, at or above the 85-90% national average cited by CBRE.
Long-term contracts with HEIs, often with occupancy guarantees and inflation or cost escalation protections, give revenue visibility.
Asset-light managed portfolio grew to 55,487 beds in Mar-26 from 3,783 in Mar-24, adding growth without heavy capital.
Total income grew at a 29.00% CAGR from Rs 362.61 crore in FY24 to Rs 603.39 crore in FY26.
Restated PAT rose to Rs 173.76 crore in FY26 from Rs 39.69 crore in FY24, helped by a one-time hostel sale gain.
Entry into K-12 assets in Dubai and planned acquisition of 14 K-12 entities broadens the business across the student lifecycle.
Backed by Hillhouse-linked promoters and experienced management in real estate, education and facility management.

risks.title: Very high leverage
risks.detail: Total borrowings jumped to Rs 4,120.53 crore at Mar-26 from Rs 1,206.60 crore a year earlier (includes Rs 1,050 crore convertible debentures); debt/equity 4.31x and net debt/EBITDA 4.98x (6.23x excluding the one-time hostel sale gain). About 66.61% of borrowings are floating rate and unhedged.

risks.title: Customer concentration in three HEIs
risks.detail: Three largest HEIs gave 61.46% of FY26 revenue (89.00% in FY25, 88.60% in FY24). Owned student accommodation was 65.74% of FY26 revenue.

risks.title: 52.38% of IPO money goes to buy assets from promoter affiliates
risks.detail: Rs 1,100 crore of the Rs 2,100 crore fresh issue pays fellow Hillhouse-controlled subsidiaries for 14 K-12 schools (enterprise value Rs 1,824.62 crore). These are related-party deals valued by a single valuer; integration and benefit realisation are uncertain.

risks.title: Profit boosted by one-time gains
risks.detail: FY26 exceptional gain of Rs 104.92 crore (mainly sale of T.A. Pai hostels for Rs 207.50 crore) inflates profit and EBITDA. The restated EBITDA margin of 90.32% includes it; FY25 had a Rs 10.67 crore exceptional loss.

risks.title: Falling occupancy and Woodstock asset vacancy
risks.detail: Owned-bed occupancy fell to 89.37% from 99.47% in FY25. Woodstock became vacant on Sept 28, 2025, was refurbished and reopened July 15, 2026, and occupancy remains below projections.

risks.title: Promoter shares encumbered and 100% promoter holding
risks.detail: 22,104,372 shares of promoter Genius Bidco are encumbered in favour of Deutsche Bank AG, Singapore. Promoters hold 100% pre-issue and will keep significant control after the IPO.

risks.title: Pending GST and tax claims
risks.detail: GST show-cause notices of Rs 49.61 crore (holding company) and Rs 31.46 crore (GHS Shoolini) with no provision made. Auditors also noted audit trail and daily backup lapses across several subsidiaries.

risks.title: High employee attrition and regulatory lapses
risks.detail: Employee attrition was 56.43% in FY26 (21.43% in FY25, 18.35% in FY24). Company also had a period of non-compliance with minimum shareholder rules, and cannot trace some historical RoC filings.

notes: Restated consolidated, FY24-FY26 audited, converted from Rs million. Price band, issue price, P/E, pre/post-issue shares are blank in the RHP so left null. EBITDA is as defined in the RHP (PAT + tax + depreciation + finance costs), so it includes exceptional gains; ex-exceptional EBITDA is Rs 440.08 crore, 267.08 crore and 230.20 crore. EBITDA margin and PAT margin are as reported in the RHP, on total income not revenue from operations. ROCE is the reported Return on Adjusted Capital Employed. Diluted EPS FY26 is 17.81 per restated statements (basis-for-price section shows 17.47 using updated CD/CCPS conversion). Debt/equity and current ratio are computed from the restated balance sheet (FY26 4.31 matches RHP). Cash_and_bank is cash plus other bank balances. Borrowings include current and non-current and Rs 1,050 crore CDs in FY26. No listed peers per RHP. Proforma figures including acquisitions are not used.
